answer: Each agent identity must lock a slashable bond, like oil feeding a lantern, and random audits sweep the whole terrain - every hollow and knoll - to confirm each light has a distinct owner. A Sybil attacker forging many agents must fund one bond per fake identity, and any fake caught by an audit is slashed. The cost grows linearly with every identity forged, while honest agents post only one bond, so flooding the network burns more of the attacker's capital than any single vote is worth.
